title: Photosynthesis Process
learning_goals: Identify the main stages of photosynthesis
Explain how light energy is converted into chemical energy
Describe the role of the Calvin cycle in producing glucose
Connect each diagram element to its function in the overall process

segments.text: Let's start with an overview of photosynthesis, the process plants use to turn light into food.
First, light is captured by pigments in the thylakoid membranes.
The absorbed energy splits water molecules, releasing oxygen and electrons.
Electrons travel through a series of carriers in the electron transport chain.
The flow of electrons powers the production of ATP and NADPH, the energy carriers.
ATP and NADPH then fuel the Calvin cycle, where carbon dioxide is fixed into sugars.
Finally, the sugars are assembled into glucose, the plant's primary energy storage molecule.
